title: S2WTM: Spherical Sliced-Wasserstein Autoencoder for Topic Modeling
task: Neural topic modelling without posterior collapse
problem: VAE topic models with von Mises-Fisher priors suffer posterior collapse because the KL term shrinks; Gaussian latents behave poorly in high dimensions.
architecture: Deterministic encoder maps BoW to the unit hypersphere (L2 normalisation); the aggregated posterior is aligned with a spherical prior (vMF, mixture of vMF, or uniform, chosen as a hyperparameter) by the Spherical Sliced-Wasserstein distance; softmax decoder whose weights give the topic-word matrix; hyperparameters tuned with Bayesian optimisation in OCTIS.
metrics: LLM rating and intrusion (Stammbach et al.)
key_results: Highest NPMI on all seven datasets (e.g. BBC 0.252, SS 0.146, DBLP 0.133).
CV is highest except M10 (0.492 vs ECRTM 0.516) and 20NG (0.723 vs 0.750 for DVAE-RSVI-TM).
Highest wI-C diversity on all datasets; median of 5 runs with K equal to the number of labels.
strengths: Avoids KL-driven posterior collapse while keeping hyperspherical geometry.
Broad evaluation: 12 baselines, 7 datasets, extrinsic, qualitative and LLM-based evaluation.

limitations.text: Spherical Radon transforms make SSW costly as the number of projections grows; LLM-based evaluation may be biased.
K is fixed to the number of gold labels, so sensitivity to K is not covered in the main tables.
